readme:
# Claude Code

Anthropic's Claude Code, connected to your editor. In Diode the extension runs in terminal mode: `claude` opens in a terminal tab next to your code, and the extension hosts the IDE connection that `claude` uses to see what you are looking at.

You need the `claude` CLI installed and on your `PATH` (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) and your own Claude account — you sign in inside `claude`. Diode neither resells nor proxies the service.

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version and verified to work in Diode.

## What works in Diode

Click **✻ Claude Code** in the status bar, or run `Claude Code: Open in Terminal`, and `claude` starts in a terminal tab to the right of the editor. `/ide` in `claude` shows Diode as connected. From then on `claude` knows the file you are in and the text you select, `Ctrl+Alt+K` inserts an @-mention of the file and the selected lines into the prompt, and `claude` can read the editor's diagnostics — the errors and warnings your language servers report. A `claude` you start by hand in any Diode terminal connects the same way.

## What does not

The chat panel is a webview, and Diode does not implement webviews: `Open in New Tab`, `Open in New Window`, `Open in Side Bar` and `Alt+K` do nothing — use the terminal and `Ctrl+Alt+K`. Proposed edits are not opened as a diff tab to accept or reject yet; answer the permission prompt inside `claude`. `Ctrl+Esc` reaches Diode only in terminals that speak the kitty keyboard protocol; elsewhere use the status bar item or the command palette.
